---
rg: 2
id: bounded-exponent-non-mf-from-corona-burnside
kind: route
title: An MF embedding would give an infinite bounded-exponent corona subgroup
target: infinite-fg-bounded-exponent-groups-are-non-mf
requires:
  - operator-norm-restricted-burnside
---

**Non-MF.**  Let `G` be infinite, generated by `m` elements, of exponent `N`,
and suppose `G` were MF. Then there is an injective homomorphism

```text
G  ->  U(Q)
```

into the unitary group of some norm matrix corona. Its image is an
`m`-generated subgroup of `U(Q)` of exponent dividing `N`, and it is infinite
because the map is injective and `G` is infinite. That contradicts
`operator-norm-restricted-burnside`. Hence `G` is not MF.

**Full MF radical in the simple case.**  Let `G` in addition be simple, and
let `rho : G -> U(Q)` be any homomorphism into any norm matrix corona. Its
image is `m`-generated of exponent dividing `N`, hence **finite** by
`operator-norm-restricted-burnside`. Now `ker rho` is normal, so by
simplicity it is `1` or `G`. If it were `1`, then `rho` would be injective
and the infinite group `G` would embed in a finite group, which is absurd.
Therefore `ker rho = G` and `rho` is trivial. As `Q` and `rho` were
arbitrary,

```text
Rad_MF(G) = intersection over all rho of ker rho = G.
```

Note the second conclusion does **not** follow from the first: non-MF says
some homomorphism fails to be injective, whereas the full-radical statement
needs every homomorphism to be trivial, and both are drawn here from the same
prerequisite rather than from each other.

Simplicity is used only for the second conclusion. Nothing in either argument
touches a trace, a normalized Hilbert--Schmidt norm, a rank, a corner, a
Kazhdan projection or a compression.
